source.author: verg
source.text: Praeterea, si qua est Heleno prudentia, vati si qua fides, animum si veris implet Apollo, unum illud tibi, nate dea, proque omnibus unum praedicam, et repetens iterumque iterumque monebo:
source.text_original: 'Praeterea, si qua est Heleno prudentia, vati / si qua fides, animum si veris implet Apollo, / unum illud tibi, nate dea, proque omnibus unum / praedicam, et repetens iterumque iterumque monebo: /
source.text_english: Moreover, if Helenus has any wisdom, if a prophet is worthy of any trust, if Apollo fills my mind with truth, this one thing alone I shall proclaim to you, son of a goddess, this one thing in place of all, and I shall warn you again and again, repeating it over and over:

reuse.author: lact
reuse.text: uereor enim ne paulatim consuetudo et iucunditas earum rerum sicut fieri solet in animum tuum irrepat, ideoque te moneo et repetens iterumque iterumque monebo, ne oblectamenta ista terrae pro magnis aut ueris bonis habere te credas, quae sunt non tantum fallacia, quia dubia, uerum etiam insidiosa, quia dulcia.
reuse.text_original: uereor enim ne paulatim consuetudo et iucunditas earum rerum sicut fieri solet in animum tuum irrepat, ideoque te moneo et repetens iterum(que) iterumque monebo, ne oblectamenta ista terrae pro magnis aut ueris bonis habere te credas, quae sunt non tantum fallacia, quia dubia, uerum etiam insidiosa, quia dulcia.
reuse.text_english: For I fear that little by little habit and the pleasantness of these things may creep into your mind, as is usually the case; and so I warn you, and, repeating it again and again, I shall warn you again and again, not to suppose that those earthly delights are to be regarded as great or true goods, for they are not only deceptive, because uncertain, but also treacherous, because sweet.
